rows.current_text: description: "Use this skill whenever asked about UAE Corporate Tax for freelancers, sole establishments, or small businesses. Trigger on phrases like \"how much tax do I pay in UAE\", \"corporate tax UAE\", \"CT return\", \"FTA\", \"small business relief\", \"free zone tax\", \"qualifying free zone person\", \"AED 375,000\", \"9% tax\", \"taxable income UAE\", \"corporate tax registration\", \"UAE tax return\", \"self-employed tax UAE\", \"freelancer tax Dubai\", \"EmaraTax\", or any question about computing or filing UAE corporate tax. This skill covers the 0%/9% rate structure, small business relief (revenue not exceeding AED 3M), qualifying free zone person rules, deductible and non-deductible expenses, transfer pricing, registration requirements, and filing deadlines. Wages are outside Corporate Tax; natural-person business scope has a turnover test. ALWAYS read this skill before touching any UAE corporate tax work."

rows.current_text: 1. **Decide whether the person is a Taxable Person.** A resident juridical person, including a free zone company, is within Article 11, subject to Article 4 exemptions. A natural person is one only if their business turnover is more than AED 1,000,000 in the calendar year, not counting wages, personal investment income or real estate investment income. Check exemptions (government entities, qualifying public benefit entities, qualifying funds and others under Article 4) and refer them out. ([Cabinet Decision No. 49 of 2023](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/05-06-2023/3/Cabinet%20Decision%20No.%2049%20of%202023%20-%20for%20publishing.pdf))

rows.current_text: 4. **Test Small Business Relief** for a resident person. Revenue must be AED 3,000,000 or less in this period *and in every previous period*. rows.current_text: **Wage exclusion from Corporate Tax.** Cabinet Decision 49/2023 excludes a natural person's Wage from Corporate Tax; a natural person's Wage is outside it "regardless of the amount of Turnover". There is no Corporate Tax calculation or Corporate Tax return on those wages. This does not determine a worker's foreign-country obligations or social deductions.

rows.current_text: **What counts as a wage.** The official definition is wide: "the wage that is given to the employee in consideration of their services under the employment contract, whether in cash or in kind, payable annually, monthly, weekly, daily, hourly, or by piece-meal, and includes all allowances, and bonuses in addition to any other benefits provided for, in the employment contract or in accordance with the applicable legislation in the State". Allowances, bonuses, benefits in kind and benefits due under UAE legislation (such as the statutory end-of-service gratuity) all fall inside it.

rows.current_text: **Employee or not is a question of fact.** The FTA says "whether a natural person is an employee and earns a salary or other form of remuneration as such, is a question of fact to be determined on a case-by-case basis". A person working under an employment contract is paid a Wage. A person who works for themselves and is not employed by the payer is running a Business, and if that person's business turnover exceeds AED 1,000,000 in a calendar year, that person is within natural-person Corporate Tax scope; apply registration and relief rules before calculating tax. The payer withholds nothing either way; the obligation is the contractor's own.

rows.current_text: **Case 5: health insurance and accommodation, VAT-registered employer.** An employer buys family health cover for an employee with a spouse and four children (ages 4, 9, 14 and 19) and, from October 2026, pays for a serviced apartment for the employee. Input tax on the cover for the employee, spouse and the three children under 18 is recoverable under exception (3). The cover for the 19-year-old is outside exception (3), so its input tax is blocked unless another exception applies. A serviced apartment is excluded from the residential-building definition. In this example assume its supplier makes a standard-rated taxable supply; the exclusion itself does not establish registration or every other VAT condition. Input tax on the October 2026 serviced-apartment charge is blocked unless a MOHRE decision or directive makes that accommodation mandatory, or a contract or documented policy provides it and every condition of case 3 of FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026 is met (or case 4, for a new employee, up to 30 days). If the employee could take a housing allowance instead, or the apartment is part of the ordinary package, it fails case 3. Had the employer instead leased an ordinary residential flat for more than six months (or to a tenant holding an Emirates ID card), the lease would be exempt: there would be no input tax on the rent, and the Article 53 change would not arise.

rows.current_text: **Case 1: mandatory registration.** A Dubai mainland trading LLC, not registered, has taxable supplies of AED 390,000 in the 12 months to 30 June 2026. That exceeds AED 375,000, so it must apply within 30 days of becoming required to register. The FTA registers it from the first day of the month after the month in which it became required to register, whether or not it applies, and it owes VAT on its taxable supplies from that date. A late application is a penalty of AED 10,000.
